memory_lessons.applicability: For this stencil campaign, explicit SIMD and scalar pointer traversal have different observed outcomes, but their code changes differ too, so the measurements do not isolate a single cause.
memory_lessons.claim: The scalar pointer-traversal candidate was valid at 0.4530 s versus the 0.4575 s baseline; a guarded OpenMP SIMD candidate using pointer traversal was valid at 0.0799 s. These measurements motivate testing SIMD on indexed accesses, but do not establish that the directive alone caused the speed difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this indexed-loop SIMD formulation against the pointer-based SIMD candidate under the same official settings.

proposal.hypothesis: A guarded OpenMP SIMD directive on the existing indexed x-loop, with only the row-base calculation factored out, may expose independent contiguous-x work without requiring pointer alignment or an ISA assumption. This contrasts with the measured scalar pointer-traversal candidate, which was near baseline, and tests whether explicit SIMD works with indexed stencil accesses rather than relying on pointer traversal.

retained: Factor the flattened z/y row base once while retaining indexed stencil accesses and contiguous x traversal.
Apply omp simd only when _OPENMP is at least 201307; otherwise compile the scalar loop.
Do not add alignment clauses, ISA assumptions, threading, or spatial or temporal blocking; preserve the arithmetic order and existing boundaries.
